claim: In daily locked-rate data on 30-year conforming mortgages from January 2017 to September 2026 (2,434 days), borrowers with credit scores of 740 or more who put down less than 20% (loan-to-value above 80) locked rates only 0.065 points higher on average than those putting down 20% or more, and the gap never exceeded 0.173 points. Holding the down payment at 20% or more, borrowers with scores below 680 locked 0.343 points higher than those at 740 or more, about 5.3 times the down-payment gap, and the credit gap was larger on 99.2% of days. On 2026-09-29 the three rates were 7.268%, 7.331% and 7.529%. The main price of a small down payment is mortgage insurance and a bigger balance, not the rate. This is history, not a forecast.

Use only dates on which all three have a numeric value (2017-01-03 through 2026-09-29). Count of those dates.

Unrounded mean_credit_gap / unrounded mean_ltv_gap, rounded to 0.1.

Daily Optimal Blue 30-year fixed conforming locked-rate indices (percent): OBMMIC30YFLVLE80FGE740 (LTV <= 80, FICO >= 740), OBMMIC30YFLVGT80FGE740 (LTV > 80, FICO >= 740), OBMMIC30YFLVLE80FLT680 (LTV <= 80, FICO < 680). Use only dates on which all three have a numeric value (2017-01-03 through 2026-09-29). Share of those dates where (LT680 - GE740, both LTV<=80) > (LTV>80 - LTV<=80, both FICO>=740), times 100, rounded to 0.1.

assumptions: Index averages of actual locks are used as the rate a typical borrower in each bucket receives; the buckets differ in other traits (points paid, loan size, lender mix) that the indices do not hold constant.
The comparison covers conforming 30-year fixed loans only; mortgage insurance premiums, which loans above 80 LTV generally require, are not in the rate and not measured here.
